title: Cascade Utility Prioritization (CUP): capacity-aware RICE + latency-cost surface
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: Problem: As we scale Redwood Dedicated and Private, classic RICE/ICE scoring underweights capacity constraints and latency budget impacts. Teams are shipping features that score high on R/I but materially increase tail latency or reserved capacity cost for high-throughput workloads. Goal: introduce a prioritization surface ("CUP") that augments RICE with a capacity and latency-cost penalty so roadmap decisions reflect both customer value and production economics. This ticket proposes the scoring model, data inputs, a small pilot on 6 candidate initiatives, and acceptance criteria for rolling CUP into the cycle planning playbook.
scoring_formula: CUP_score = Base_RICE * Utilization_Adjustment * LatencyCost_Adjustment. Where Base_RICE = (Reach * Impact * Confidence) / Effort. Utilization_Adjustment = 1 - min(0.6, Projected_peak_reserved_capacity_increase / Capacity_threshold). LatencyCost_Adjustment = 1 / (1 + normalized_token_latency_cost_increase). Scores are normalized to 0-100 for display.
sample_calculation: Example initiative A: Reach=0.12 (12% MAU), Impact=6, Confidence=0.7, Effort=8 -> Base_RICE = (0.12*6*0.7)/8 = 0.063. Projected reserved capacity increase = 15% against threshold 40% -> Utilization_Adjustment = 1 - 0.15 = 0.85. Normalized latency-cost increase = 0.12 -> LatencyCost_Adjustment = 1/(1+0.12)=0.893. CUP_score_raw = 0.063*0.85*0.893=0.0478 -> normalized display score = 47.8. Interpretation: despite good reach/impact, capacity and latency penalties reduce priority relative to features with lighter production cost.
acceptance_criteria: Defined CUP scoring doc with formula, thresholds, and normalization rules (this ticket)
Instrumentation queries and dashboard panels showing projected capacity/%cost delta per initiative
Pilot applied to 6 initiatives in Cycle 2026-W11 with documented before/after prioritization order
Stakeholder sign-off from Eng infra, Runtime, Product, and Finance on thresholds and knobs
Updated cycle planning playbook (Confluence) describing when to apply CUP vs standard RICE
data_sources: console per-route latency and P95/P99 traces
notes: Trade-offs: CUP penalizes high-value product work that increases infra cost; to avoid systemic bias toward low-cost features we cap the Utilization_Adjustment penalty at 60% and introduce a 'strategic override' flag for high-strategic bets (requires exec approval). We also normalize Reach differently for enterprise-only features. Implementation plan keeps RICE inputs unchanged for product teams; CUP coefficients are computed centrally and injected into prioritization UI.
implementation_plan: 1) Instrument cost & latency projections (ENG-4123) -> 2 weeks. 2) Implement CUP calculator endpoint and UI columns in planning tool -> 1 sprint. 3) Run 2-week pilot with 6 initiatives and collect metrics -> 2 weeks. 4) Post-mortem and playbook update -> 1 week.
risk_mitigation: Bias to low-cost work: strategic_override with documented rationale
Data quality: roll forward with conservative defaults when telemetry missing
Model gaming: results audit logs and quarterly reviews by Finance and Runtime
